subsystems.name: Damage sensing
subsystems.role: detect the molecular hallmarks of UV injury — DNA lesions, oxidative stress and fragmented collagen.
parts: recognition elements such as antibodies or nucleic-acid probes
a signalling circuit that triggers only above a threshold

subsystems.name: Payload and effectors
subsystems.role: make or deliver the proteins that rebuild skin: collagen, elastin and the enzymes that cross-link them.
parts: messenger RNA or gene circuits encoding collagen and elastin
engineered fibroblasts or cell-free enzyme systems

subsystems.name: Targeting and residence
subsystems.role: keep the units in the dermis, where fibroblasts sit, rather than drifting into blood or lymph.
parts: surface ligands binding dermal matrix proteins
a designed degradation or retrieval mechanism

subsystems.name: Power and control
subsystems.role: supply energy and give a way to switch the system on, off or out.
parts: chemistry fuelled by glucose and ATP already in tissue

subsystems.name: Safety and immune handling
subsystems.role: avoid rejection, unwanted immune activation, or uncontrolled cell growth.

buildSteps.title: Choose the biological effect
buildSteps.detail: Decide what to rebuild — for photoaged skin, replacing fragmented collagen and elastin in the dermis, a layer a few millimetres thick, is the target.

buildSteps.title: Design the effector molecules
buildSteps.detail: Engineer messenger RNA or gene circuits that instruct skin cells to produce the right collagen and elastin types, using the chemistry already proven in messenger-RNA medicines.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the payload
buildSteps.detail: Produce the nucleic acids or proteins by cell-free synthesis or engineered cell culture, then purify and check each batch.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate and target
buildSteps.detail: Package the payload in lipid nanoparticles or polymer carriers, and decorate the surface with ligands that bind dermal matrix so the units stay where they are needed.

buildSteps.title: Add sensing and control
buildSteps.detail: Attach recognition elements for damage markers and a switch — chemical or external — so activity can be stopped.

buildSteps.title: Test in skin models
buildSteps.detail: Try it first on lab-grown human skin equivalents and excised skin, measuring new collagen, mechanical strength and immune response.

buildSteps.title: Test in whole animals
buildSteps.detail: Move to animal models of UV damage and scarring to see whether the units persist, migrate or cause inflammation.

buildSteps.title: Deliver and trial in humans
buildSteps.detail: If safe, deliver by microneedle patch or injection and run staged clinical trials with long follow-up, since a resident implant must be monitored for years.

prerequisites.tech: Targeted delivery of large payloads into skin cells
prerequisites.why: lipid nanoparticles and microneedle patches work for vaccines and some drugs, but dermal collagen expression at useful scale is unproven.

prerequisites.tech: Control of collagen and elastin production in living tissue
prerequisites.why: we can express proteins in cells, but turning that into correctly structured, correctly cross-linked skin is much harder than producing one protein.
today's nanoparticles carry cargo but cannot sense, decide and act on their own; molecular assemblers remain theory.
the body tends to attack or wall off foreign material, which is fatal to a device meant to reside for decades.
anything left in the body must be easily deactivated and removed if it misbehaves.

pathway.milestone: messenger-RNA and gene-editing medicines reach the clinic for other conditions
pathway.unlocks: a proven route to instruct human cells to make chosen proteins.

pathway.milestone: skin-targeted gene and protein therapies show they can change dermal structure in trials
pathway.unlocks: treatments for scarring and photoaging that act biologically rather than by ablation.

pathway.milestone: sensing carriers that release a payload only where damage markers are present
pathway.unlocks: responsive, self-limiting therapy without a resident machine.

pathway.milestone: engineered cells or cell-free systems that persist in skin and maintain repair over years
pathway.unlocks: the dermal-repair idea in a realistic form — if immune rejection and long-term safety are solved.
